body.x: Worker’s High (CEO ChoongHee Kim) announced its participation in the Global Media Meetup on September 2. The event, co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media Ubergizmo, highlighted CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and participants, aiming to provide Korean startups with global exposure and business opportunities.

Worker’s High operates Flagshop, an AI-based uncrewed retail solution designed for spaces such as offices, campuses, and shared facilities. The platform optimizes product recommendations by integrating customer data, purchase history, time, and weather. Data accumulated through Flagshop undergoes AI-driven analysis to enhance personalized offerings.

Flagshop functions as a practical retail channel for consumers while serving as a product-testing and distribution platform for manufacturers. With hot, cold, and ambient storage options, it offers a variety of beverages, bread, salads, fruits, and more. Buyers of Flagshop can customize the exterior to match their interior designs, enhancing the aesthetic appeal.

The solution has garnered recognition with awards, including the 2025 NextRise Innovation Award (AI Core) and selection for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ TIPS program (2023, AI Curation). The company also holds 12 patents and seven registered trademarks.

Currently deployed at more than 150 B2B sites, Flagshop recently expanded into residential channels through an uncrewed retail rental agreement with Homes Company. The company plans overseas pilot deployments in Vietnam and Japan.

At CES 2026, Worker’s High will present Flagshop as an integrated system that combines modular IoT devices for hot, cold, and ambient storage, sensor interfaces, remote control software, and AI curation. These features enable real-time sales and inventory analysis, automated POG (planogram) optimization, and auto-ordering. According to the company, this system has achieved an average sales increase of 28%, enabled three-second kiosk payments, demonstrated demand forecasting accuracy of 91.7%, and achieved auto-order accuracy of 87.6%, resulting in over an 85% reduction in operating time and cost. Retention rates exceed 80%, with client retention at around 98%.

Design highlights include a showcase-style open structure, a 32-inch touchscreen interface, and a space-customized exterior. Flagshop also won the 2024 Red Dot Design Award. Its D2C infrastructure provides manufacturers with real-world product testing, GTM strategies, and data reports, differentiating it from vending machines or basic uncrewed systems.

body.cap: Nathan JH. Moon, COO of Worker’s High, delivers a presentation at the Global Media Meetup with Ubergizmo held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: By integrating AI-based demand forecasting and display optimization, Flagshop reduces food overproduction and waste, while last-mile purchases from urban idle spaces minimize transport and packaging. Local businesses also gain data-driven demand insights to overcome initial distribution barriers.

Worker’s High plans to enhance Flagshop with lightweight, low-power hardware, expanded 1–3 door lineups, new beverage and multi-type models, upgraded POG automation engines, a full-scale retail media platform, and ESG reporting standardization.

In Japan and Vietnam, the company will roll out Flagshop in hotels and residences, followed by offices and campuses, while securing maintenance, logistics, and partnerships, as well as certifications (PSE/TELEC, HACCP). It also plans to present on-site PoC packages—including installation testing, retail media trials, and data reporting—at global events such as RetailTech Japan, CEATEC, FHA Singapore, Smart City expos, and Vietnam Foodexpo, alongside signing MOUs with payment, logistics, and operations partners to accelerate commercialization.

body.cap: Nathan JH. Moon, COO of Worker’s High, and Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo, take a commemorative photo at the Global Media Meetup held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 2 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.
